1.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
1.solution:
Maximum acceleration in SHM is \(a_{\max} = \omega^{2}A\). With equal amplitude, \(a_{\max} \propto \omega^{2}\):
\[\frac{(a_{\max})_{1}}{(a_{\max})_{2}} = \left(\frac{\omega_{1}}{\omega_{2}}\right)^{2} = \left(\frac{300}{3000}\right)^{2} = \left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{10^{2}}.\]

2.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
2.solution:
From the figure, point P lies on the line of the wires, at distance \(r\) from the nearer wire and \(r + 2r = 3r\) from the farther wire; both currents are in the same direction so at P the two fields add:
\[B_{net} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi r} + \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi(3r)} = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi}\left(\frac{1}{r} + \frac{1}{3r}\right) = \frac{\mu_{0}I}{2\pi}\cdot\frac{4}{3r} = \frac{2}{3}\frac{\mu_{0}I}{\pi r}.\]
2.note: Stem prints the current as 'T'; it is the current I (the options use I). Figure needed to fix P at distances r and 3r.

3.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
3.solution:
By Stefan's law \(E = \sigma A T^{4}\), so \(E \propto A T^{4}\). Length and breadth halved \(\Rightarrow A \to A/4\); temperature \(27^\circ\text{C}=300\) K to \(327^\circ\text{C}=600\) K, ratio 2.
\[\frac{E_{2}}{E_{1}} = \frac{1}{4}\times(2)^{4} = \frac{16}{4} = 4 \Rightarrow E_{2} = 4E.\]

4.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
4.solution:
Dipping one end in water makes a closed pipe. Second overtone of a closed pipe is the 5th harmonic: \(f = \dfrac{5v}{4L'}\), where \(L'=1.5-x\) is the air-column length.
\[330 = \frac{5\times330}{4(1.5-x)} \Rightarrow 1.5-x = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25 \Rightarrow x = 0.25\ \text{m}.\]

5.solution:
For \(A = \dfrac{B^{\alpha}C^{\beta}}{D^{\gamma}E^{\delta}}\), the maximum fractional errors add with the powers as coefficients (all positive):
\[\frac{\Delta A}{A} = \alpha\frac{\Delta B}{B} + \beta\frac{\Delta C}{C} + \gamma\frac{\Delta D}{D} + \delta\frac{\Delta E}{E},\]
so the maximum percentage error is \((\alpha b + \beta c + \gamma d + \delta e)\%\).

6.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
6.solution:
At resonance \(I = \dfrac{V_{R}}{R} = \dfrac{200}{800} = 0.25\) A and \(X_{L} = X_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}\).
\[X_{C} = \frac{1}{250\times2\times10^{-6}} = 2000\ \Omega.\]
Voltage across inductance:
\[V_{L} = IX_{L} = 0.25\times2000 = 500\ \text{V}.\]

7.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
7.solution:
For an adiabatic process \(P^{1-\gamma}T^{\gamma} = \text{const}\), i.e. \(P \propto T^{\gamma/(\gamma-1)}\). For a rigid diatomic gas \(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\):
\[c = \frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1} = \frac{7/5}{2/5} = \frac{7}{2} = 3.5.\]
7.note: Stem 'P \proptoT^{c}' is a glued extraction of P \propto T^{c}.

Flux in Q when P carries \(I_{P} = 1.8\) A:

10.solution:
Three vectors form a (closed) triangle only if one is the sum of the other two, which requires them to be coplanar (scalar triple product zero).
\[\overrightarrow{A}\cdot(\overrightarrow{B}\times\overrightarrow{C}) = \begin{vmatrix} 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & -3 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 3(-12+5)+2(4-10)+1(-1+6) = -21-12+5 = -28 \neq 0.\]
Since the triple product is non-zero the vectors are not coplanar, so they form no triangle.

11.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
11.solution:
At the midpoint each wire is at the same distance. Same direction: fields subtract, \(B_{1}-B_{2} = 8\times10^{-6}\). Opposite direction: fields add, \(B_{1}+B_{2} = 3.2\times10^{-5}\). Dividing,
\[\frac{I_{1}-I_{2}}{I_{1}+I_{2}} = \frac{8\times10^{-6}}{3.2\times10^{-5}} = 0.25 \Rightarrow 0.75I_{1} = 1.25I_{2} \Rightarrow \frac{I_{2}}{I_{1}} = \frac{0.75}{1.25} = \frac{3}{5}.\]
11.note: Field values dropped leading digits in extraction; from the AK solution they are 8 x 10^-6 T (same direction) and 3.2 x 10^-5 T (reversed).

If the direction of \(I_{2}\) is reversed, the field becomes \(3.2\times10^{-5}\text{ }T\). The ratio of \(I_{2}\) to \(I_{1}\) is

12.solution: Initial angular speed \(\omega_{0} = 2\pi f = 2\pi\cdot\dfrac{240}{60} = 8\pi\ \text{rad/s}\). Brought to rest in 20 s: \(\alpha = \dfrac{8\pi}{20} = \dfrac{2\pi}{5}\ \text{rad/s}^{2}\). Moment of inertia of disc \(I = \dfrac{1}{2}MR^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(25)(0.2)^{2} = 0.5\ \text{kg}\,\text{m}^{2}\). Torque \(\tau = I\alpha = 0.5\times\dfrac{2\pi}{5} = 0.2\pi\ \text{N}\,\text{m}\), and \(F = \dfrac{\tau}{R} = \dfrac{0.2\pi}{0.2} = \pi\ \text{N}\).

13.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
13.solution:
Resultant intensity \(I_{R} = I_{1}+I_{2}+2\sqrt{I_{1}I_{2}}\cos\phi\), with \(I_{1}=I,\ I_{2}=9I\).
At P (\(\phi=\pi/2\)): \(I_{P} = I+9I+0 = 10I\).
At Q (\(\phi=\pi\)): \(I_{Q} = 10I - 2\sqrt{9I^{2}} = 10I-6I = 4I\).
Difference \(= 10I-4I = 6I\).

14.solution: NAND (and NOR) gates are universal gates: any logic function can be built using only NAND gates. Among the options, NAND is the universal gate.

15.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
15.solution:
For an ideal gas \(PV=nRT\) with \(n = \dfrac{m}{M}\) gives \(\rho = \dfrac{PM}{RT}\), so \(\rho \propto \dfrac{P}{T}\).
\[\rho' = \rho_{0}\cdot\frac{P'}{P_{0}}\cdot\frac{T_{0}}{T'} = \rho_{0}\cdot\frac{3P_{0}}{P_{0}}\cdot\frac{T_{0}}{2T_{0}} = \frac{3}{2}\rho_{0}.\]

16.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
16.solution: For a semiconductor the resistivity DECREASES with rising temperature (more carriers thermally excited). The graph that shows \(\rho\) falling steeply then levelling with \(T\) is graph (C) in the figure set, which corresponds to option A = '(C)'.
16.note: Four candidate graphs are figures; the question asks which one is correct. The decreasing graph (labelled C in the stem) is the answer, matching option A's text '(C)'.

17.solution:
Fundamental \(n = \dfrac{1}{2l r}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi\rho}}\) (since linear mass density \(m = \pi r^{2}\rho\)).
1st overtone of wire 1 (2nd harmonic): \(n_{1} = \dfrac{2}{2l_{1}r_{1}}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi\rho}} = \dfrac{1}{l_{1}r_{1}}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi\rho}}\).
2nd overtone of wire 2 (3rd harmonic): \(n_{2} = \dfrac{3}{2l_{2}r_{2}}\sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\pi\rho}}\).
Setting \(n_{1}=n_{2}\): \(\dfrac{1}{l_{1}r_{1}} = \dfrac{3}{2l_{2}r_{2}}\Rightarrow 2l_{2}r_{2} = 3l_{1}r_{1}\). With \(r_{1}=2r_{2}\):
\[\frac{l_{1}}{l_{2}} = \frac{2r_{2}}{3r_{1}} = \frac{2r_{2}}{6r_{2}} = \frac{1}{3}.\]

18.subtopic: Classification, Curie's Law, Hysteresis, and Shielding
18.solution: For a diamagnetic substance the susceptibility \(\chi\) is small, negative and essentially independent of temperature — a horizontal line slightly below the axis. That is graph (A) in the figure set, which corresponds to option C = '(A)'.
18.note: Four candidate graphs are figures; the temperature-independent (flat, negative) line is the diamagnetic one, matching option C's text '(A)'.

19.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
19.solution:
For a thin liquid film of thickness \(t\) between the plates, the adhesive (separating) force is \(F = \dfrac{2TA}{t}\). With \(t = \dfrac{V}{A}\):
\[F = \frac{2TA}{V/A} = \frac{2TA^{2}}{V} \Rightarrow T = \frac{FV}{2A^{2}}.\]

20.subtopic: LC Oscillations, Transformer, and AC Generator
20.solution:
From the figure, \(L = 16\) mH and \(C = 10\ \mu\text{F}\). Charge oscillates as \(q = q_{0}\cos\omega_{0}t\) (max energy at \(t=0\)); current \(i = i_{0}\sin\omega_{0}t\) is first maximum when \(\omega_{0}t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), i.e. \(t = \dfrac{\pi}{2\omega_{0}}\).
\[\omega_{0} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{16\times10^{-3}\times10\times10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{16\times10^{-8}}} = 2500\ \text{rad/s}.\]
\[t = \frac{\pi}{2\times2500} = \frac{\pi}{5000} = 2\pi\times10^{-4}\ \text{s}.\]
20.note: Independently derived t = pi/(2*omega_0) with omega_0 = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(16e-3*10e-6) = 2500 rad/s, giving t = pi/5000 = 2*pi x 10^-4 s = option C. AK keyed B (2*pi x 10^-3 s) is wrong by a factor of 10 and contradicts the AK's own working (which computes 2*pi x 10^-4). Correct option C exists, so not flawed.

21.subtopic: Kinematics — Equations of Motion, Free Fall, and Graphs
21.solution:
Reading the v-t graph (areas of the rectangular segments, signs by side of the time axis):
Displacement = \((3\times2) - (2\times2) + (2\times2) - (2\times2) + (2\times2)\)... using the segment areas \(6,-2,4,-2,4\): displacement \(= 6-2+4-2+4 = 10\).
Distance = \(6+2+4+2+4 = 18\).
\[\frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{distance}} = \frac{10}{18} = \frac{5}{9}.\]
21.note: Graph read: +3 for 2 s, -2 for 1 s (areas tally to displacement 10, distance 18 per the AK segment values). Ratio 5:9.

22.solution:
The balancing length is proportional to the total wire length (same cell, same driving current). Original total length \(L\) gives balance \(\dfrac{L}{5}\). New total length \(L + \dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{3L}{2}\), so the balance length scales by \(\dfrac{3}{2}\):
\[x = \frac{L}{5}\times\frac{3}{2} = \frac{3L}{10}.\]

23.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
23.solution:
RMS current \(I = \dfrac{V}{Z} = \dfrac{220}{33} = \dfrac{20}{3}\) A. True power dissipated in R:
\[P = I^{2}R = \left(\frac{20}{3}\right)^{2}\times18 = \frac{400}{9}\times18 = 800\ \text{W}.\]

24.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
24.solution:
Going down with \(a = g/3\): apparent weight \(W_{1} = m(g-a) = m\cdot\dfrac{2g}{3} = 20\) N.
Going up with \(a = g/3\): \(W_{2} = m(g+a) = m\cdot\dfrac{4g}{3} = 2W_{1} = 40\) N.

25.solution:
From the figure: left half (area \(A/2\), full gap \(d\), \(K_{1}=4\)) is \(C_{1}\); right half is split top/bottom (each area \(A/2\), gap \(d/2\), \(K_{2}=3\) and \(K_{3}=6\)) in series. Let \(C = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_{0}}{d}\).
\[C_{1} = \frac{4(A/2)\varepsilon_{0}}{d} = 2C,\quad C_{2} = \frac{3(A/2)\varepsilon_{0}}{d/2} = 3C,\quad C_{3} = \frac{6(A/2)\varepsilon_{0}}{d/2} = 6C.\]
\(C_{2},C_{3}\) in series: \(C_{s} = \dfrac{3C\cdot6C}{9C} = 2C\). Then \(C_{eq} = C_{1} + C_{s} = 2C + 2C = 4C = \dfrac{4A\varepsilon_{0}}{d}\).

26.solution:
Emission requires a higher-to-lower transition; \(n=1\to3\) and \(n=2\to4\) are absorptions. For emissions, \(\nu \propto \left|\dfrac{1}{n_{f}^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{n_{i}^{2}}\right|\).
\(5\to3\): \(\nu \propto \dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{16}{225} \approx 0.071\).
\(2\to1\): \(\nu \propto \dfrac{1}{1}-\dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75\).
The largest frequency is the \(2\to1\) transition.

27.subtopic: Variation of g with Depth, Altitude, Density, and Latitude
27.solution:
Capillary rise \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g} \propto \dfrac{1}{g}\). At depth \(d\), \(g_{d} = g\left(1-\dfrac{d}{R}\right)\).
\[\frac{Y}{x} = \frac{g}{g_{d}} = \frac{1}{1-\frac{d}{R}} = \frac{R}{R-d} \Rightarrow Y:x = R:(R-d).\]

28.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
28.solution:
A minimum exactly in front of one slit means the path difference there equals an odd multiple of \(\lambda/2\); equivalently \(d = (2m-1)W\) where \(W = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\) is the fringe width, for \(m=1,2,3,\dots\)
Thus \(d = (2m-1)\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}\Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{d^{2}}{(2m-1)D}\), giving \(\lambda = \dfrac{d^{2}}{D},\dfrac{d^{2}}{3D},\dfrac{d^{2}}{5D},\dots\), i.e. \(\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{D},\dfrac{1}{3D},\dfrac{1}{5D},\dots\)

29.subtopic: Satellites, Orbital Motion, and Kepler's Laws
29.solution: For a circular orbit \(KE = \dfrac{GMm}{2r}\), \(PE = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}\), total \(E = -\dfrac{GMm}{2r}\). Hence \(E = \dfrac{1}{2}PE\) (half the potential energy).

30.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
30.solution: de Broglie wavelength \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p}\). Impulse equals change in momentum, so \(\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{p}\) — inversely proportional to (the) momentum/impulse.

31.solution:
By continuity \(A_{A}v_{A} = A_{B}v_{B}\), with \(A \propto R^{2}\):
\[\pi R^{2}V = \pi\left(\frac{R}{3}\right)^{2}v_{B} \Rightarrow v_{B} = \frac{R^{2}}{R^{2}/9}V = 9V.\]

32.solution:
Equal initial nuclei \(N_{0}\). \(N_{A} = N_{0}e^{-7\lambda t}\), \(N_{B} = N_{0}e^{-\lambda t}\). Require \(\dfrac{N_{B}}{N_{A}} = e\):
\[\frac{e^{-\lambda t}}{e^{-7\lambda t}} = e^{6\lambda t} = e^{1} \Rightarrow 6\lambda t = 1 \Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{6\lambda}.\]

From the figure A is the midpoint of the left side, between the two \(+2q\) charges; distances: \(AB = AE = L\) (the two near \(+2q\)), and to the far \(-2q\) charges \(AC = AD = \sqrt{(2L)^{2}+L^{2}} = \sqrt{5}L\).

36.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
36.solution:
Same wire \(\Rightarrow\) constant linear density \(\lambda\); mass \(M = \lambda(2\pi R)\). MI of a ring about its axis \(I = MR^{2}\):
\[I_{P} = (2\pi r\lambda)r^{2} = 2\pi\lambda r^{3},\quad I_{Q} = (2\pi nr\lambda)(nr)^{2} = 2\pi\lambda n^{3}r^{3}.\]
\[I_{Q} = 4I_{P} \Rightarrow n^{3} = 4 \Rightarrow n = 4^{1/3} = 2^{2/3}.\]

38.solution:
Support moves as \(y = kt^{2}\) with \(k = 1\ \text{m/s}^{2}\) so acceleration \(a = \ddot{y} = 2k = 2\ \text{m/s}^{2}\) upward. Effective gravity \(g' = g+a = 12\ \text{m/s}^{2}\).
\[\frac{T_{1}^{2}}{T_{2}^{2}} = \frac{l/g}{l/g'} = \frac{g'}{g} = \frac{12}{10} = \frac{6}{5}.\]

39.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
39.solution:
Solenoid: \(L = \dfrac{\mu_{0}N^{2}A}{l} = \dfrac{\mu_{0}N^{2}\pi r^{2}}{l}\Rightarrow N^{2}r^{2} = \dfrac{Ll}{\mu_{0}\pi}\Rightarrow Nr = \sqrt{\dfrac{Ll}{\mu_{0}\pi}}\).
Wire length \(l_{0} = 2\pi Nr = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{Ll}{\mu_{0}\pi}}\), so
\[l_{0}^{2} = 4\pi^{2}\cdot\frac{Ll}{\mu_{0}\pi} = \frac{4\pi Ll}{\mu_{0}} \Rightarrow l_{0} = \left[\frac{4\pi lL}{\mu_{0}}\right]^{1/2}.\]
39.note: Wire length l0 = 2*pi*N*r = [4*pi*l*L/mu_0]^(1/2), which is option A. The AK's own derivation yields the same expression; option C as printed is garbled ([4*pi*mu_0/(LL)]^(1/2)). Correct answer A.

44.solution:
From the figure, axis YY' passes through the diameter of the top sphere and is tangent to the two lower spheres.
Top sphere (axis through diameter): \(I = \dfrac{2}{5}mr^{2}\).

47.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
47.solution:
Cylinder A: constant pressure (\(Q = nC_{p}\Delta T_{A}\)); cylinder B: constant volume (\(Q = nC_{v}\Delta T_{B}\)). Equal heat:
\[nC_{p}\Delta T_{A} = nC_{v}\Delta T_{B} \Rightarrow \Delta T_{B} = \gamma\,\Delta T_{A}.\]
For rigid diatomic gas \(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\): \(49 = \dfrac{7}{5}\Delta T_{A}\Rightarrow \Delta T_{A} = 35\) K.

48.subtopic: Refraction, Apparent Depth, and Total Internal Reflection
48.solution: Mirage, brilliance of diamond, and optical fibres all rely on total internal reflection. The apparent-vs-real depth of a pond is due to ordinary refraction (not TIR), so that is the phenomenon NOT due to TIR.

49.solution: Motional EMF \(e = B l v\), where \(l\) is the length of the side perpendicular to the velocity (the side that cuts field lines). Initially the vertical side (length = coil length) is the cutting edge. After rotating the coil \(90^\circ\) in its plane, the longer side (the breadth that was horizontal) becomes vertical and now cuts the field, giving a larger \(l\) and hence a larger EMF.
49.note: Coil is rectangular (length != breadth). Rotating 90 deg swaps which side is the cutting edge; the induced EMF e = Blv changes because l changes. The intended answer is that it is greater than the initial EMF.
